headline: Statistics finds patterns in data—making sense of many observations to reveal underlying trends
universal_truth: One data point is an anecdote; many data points reveal patterns; quantity enables insight
fun_facts: The average human has one ovary and one testicle—averages can be misleading
Correlation doesn't mean causation—ice cream sales and drowning rates both rise in summer
Florence Nightingale was a pioneering statistician who used data visualization to save lives
discussion_questions: Where do you rely on anecdotes when you need statistics?
How do you distinguish patterns from noise in your life?
What data should you be collecting but aren't?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: One person's experience is a story. A thousand people's experiences reveal a pattern. Statistics transforms many observations into insight—finding the signal in the noise, the trend in the chaos.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often make decisions based on a few examples. Why does quantity of data matter so much?
cliff.prompt: Why do statistics require many data points?

options.text: Quantity reveals patterns obscured by individual variation—single cases are misleading; only many observations expose what's typical versus exceptional
options.response: Yes. Any individual case might be unusual. Only with many cases do patterns emerge. Statistics sacrifices detail for accuracy—trading one story for a thousand data points.

options.text: More data is just more accurate
options.response: More accurate, yes, but specifically because individual variation cancels out and patterns emerge...

q1.title: Anecdote vs Data
q1.script: A friend's experience is an anecdote. Thousands of experiences are data. Anecdotes are vivid but potentially misleading. Data is boring but reliable. Know which you're using.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Anecdote vs Data"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Correlation Isn't Causation
q2.script: When two things happen together, they might not cause each other. Ice cream sales and drownings both rise in summer—but ice cream doesn't cause drowning. Summer causes both.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Statistics
q3.script: You can apply statistical thinking personally: track your patterns over time. What correlates with your good days? Bad days? Many observations reveal what single examples hide.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: One data point is an anecdote; many data points reveal patterns. Quantity enables insight. Don't trust single cases.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 302. Tomorrow, we'll explore why moving matters—exercise. Until then, notice where you're generalizing from too few examples.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Data Collection Plan - What Should You Track?
growTrack.activity: What would you like to understand about your own patterns—energy, mood, productivity, health? Design a simple tracking system. What data points would reveal useful patterns over time?
